sanskrit: stry uvāca nānilo 'gnir na varuṇo na cānye tridaśā dvija priyāḥ strīṇāṃ yathā kāmo ratiśīlā hi yoṣitaḥ
english: The woman said: Not the Wind, not Fire, not Varuṇa, nor any of the other gods, O brāhmaṇa, are as dear to women as is desire; for women are creatures given over to pleasure.

sanskrit: sahasraikā yatā nārī prāpnotīha kadā cana tathā śatasahasreṣu yadi kā cit pativratā
english: Scarcely one woman in a thousand is found here who is restrained; and among a hundred thousand, only here and there is one devoted to her husband.

sanskrit: naitā jānanti pitaraṃ na kulaṃ na ca mātaram na bhrātṝn na ca bhartāraṃ na putrān na ca devarān
english: They heed neither father nor lineage nor mother, neither brothers nor husband, neither sons nor brothers-in-law.

sanskrit: līlāyantyaḥ kulaṃ ghnanti kūlānīva saridvarāḥ doṣāṃś ca mandān mandāsu prajāpatir abhāṣata
english: Sporting in their wantonness, they destroy their families as the great rivers wear away their banks; and Prajāpati declared that such failings dwell within women of weak mind.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sa ṛṣir ekāgras tāṃ striyaṃ pratyabhāṣata āsyatāṃ ruciraṃ chandaḥ kiṃ vā kāryaṃ bravīhi me
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the sage, with collected mind, answered that woman: "As you please, be seated; or tell me—what is the task you would have done?"

sanskrit: sā strī provāca bhagavan drakṣyase deśakālataḥ vasa tāvan mahāprājña kṛtakṛtyo gamiṣyasi
english: The woman replied: "Lord, in due place and time you shall see. Dwell here a while, O greatly wise one; when your purpose is accomplished, you shall depart."

sanskrit: brahmarṣis tām athovāca sa tatheti yudhiṣṭhira vatsye 'haṃ yāvad utsāho bhavatyā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa-seer then said to her, "So be it," O Yudhiṣṭhira—"I shall dwell here as long as it pleases you; of that there is no doubt."

sanskrit: atharṣir abhisaṃprekṣya striyaṃ tāṃ jarayānvitām cintāṃ paramikāṃ bheje saṃtapta iva cābhavat
english: Then the seer, gazing upon that woman bowed down with age, fell into deep reflection and became as one consumed with care.

sanskrit: yad yad aṅgaṃ hi so 'paśyat tasyā viprarṣabhas tadā nāramat tatra tatrāsya dṛṣṭī rūpaparājitā
english: Whatever limb of hers that bull among brāhmaṇas looked upon, there his gaze found no delight, overcome by her ruined form.

sanskrit: devateyaṃ gṛhasyāsya śāpān nūnaṃ virūpitā asyāś ca kāraṇaṃ vettuṃ na yuktaṃ sahasā mayā
english: "Surely this is the deity of this house, disfigured by some curse; yet it would not be fitting for me to seek out the cause of it in haste."

sanskrit: iti cintāviṣaktasya tam arthaṃ jñātum icchataḥ vyagamat tad ahaḥśeṣaṃ manasā vyākulena tu
english: As he was thus absorbed in thought, longing to know the truth of the matter, the remainder of that day passed away while his mind was troubled.

sanskrit: atha sā strī tadovāca bhagavan paśya vai raveḥ rūpaṃ saṃdhyābhrasaṃyuktaṃ kim upasthāpyatāṃ tava
english: Then that woman said: "Lord, behold the form of the sun joined with the clouds of twilight. What shall be made ready for you?"

sanskrit: sa uvāca tadā tāṃ strīṃ snānodakam ihānaya upāsiṣye tataḥ saṃdhyāṃ vāgyato niyatendriyaḥ
english: He then said to that woman: "Bring water here for bathing; then, restrained in speech and with senses controlled, I shall attend upon the twilight rite."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atha sā strī tam uktvā tu vipram evaṃ bhavatv iti tailaṃ divyam upādāya snānaśāṭīm upānayat
english: Bhīṣma said: Then that woman, saying to the brāhmaṇa, "So be it," took up celestial oil and brought to him a bathing-cloth.

sanskrit: anujñātā ca muninā sā strī tena mahātmanā athāsya tailenāṅgāni sarvāṇy evābhyamṛkṣayat
english: And, granted leave by that great-souled sage, the woman anointed all his limbs with the oil.

sanskrit: śanaiś cotsāditas tatra snānaśālām upāgamat bhadrāsanaṃ tataś citraṃ ṛṣir anvāviśan navam
english: Gently rubbed down, he went into the bathing-chamber; and the seer then took his place upon a fine new seat richly adorned.

sanskrit: athopaviṣṭaś ca yadā tasmin bhadrāsane tadā snāpayām āsa śanakais tam ṛṣiṃ sukhahastavat divyaṃ ca vidhivac cakre sopacāraṃ munes tadā
english: And when he was seated upon that goodly seat, she bathed the seer slowly, with a gentle hand, and performed for the sage the celestial rite duly, with every attendance.

sanskrit: sa tena susukhoṣṇena tasyā hastasukhena ca vyatītāṃ rajanīṃ kṛtsnāṃ nājānāt sa mahāvrataḥ
english: By that pleasantly warm water and by the soothing touch of her hand, that man of great vows did not perceive that the whole night had passed away.

sanskrit: tata utthāya sa munis tadā paramavismitaḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi sūryaṃ ca so 'paśyad uditaṃ divi
english: Then the sage, rising up in utter amazement, beheld the sun risen in the sky in the eastern quarter.

sanskrit: tasya buddhir iyaṃ kiṃ nu mohas tattvam idaṃ bhavet athopāsya sahasrāṃśuṃ kiṃ karomīty uvāca tām
english: This thought came to him: "Is this a delusion, or is it the truth?" Then, having worshipped the thousand-rayed one, he said to her, "What shall I do?"

sanskrit: sā cāmṛtarasaprakhyam ṛṣer annam upāharat tasya svādutayānnasya na prabhūtaṃ cakāra saḥ vyagamac cāpy ahaḥśeṣaṃ tataḥ saṃdhyāgamat punaḥ
english: She set before the seer food that was like the taste of nectar; and by reason of the sweetness of that food he could not make an end of it. So the rest of the day passed away, and the twilight came again.

sanskrit: atha strī bhagavantaṃ sā supyatām ity acodayat tatra vai śayane divye tasya tasyāś ca kalpite
english: Then that woman urged the lord, saying, "Let us sleep," upon celestial couches there made ready, one for him and one for her.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca na bhadre paradāreṣu mano me saṃprasajjati uttiṣṭha bhadre bhadraṃ te svapa vai viramasva ca
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: "No, good lady; my mind does not cling to another man's wife. Rise up, good lady—blessings upon you—go to sleep, and desist."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sā tadā tena vipreṇa tathā dhṛtyā nivartitā svatantrāsmīty uvācainaṃ na dharmacchalam asti te
english: Bhīṣma said: She, thus turned back by the brāhmaṇa's firmness, said to him, "I am my own mistress; there is no deceiving of dharma in this for you."

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca nāsti svatantratā strīṇām asvatantrā hi yoṣitaḥ prajāpatimataṃ hy etan na strī svātantryam arhati
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: "Women have no independence; a woman is never her own mistress. This is the doctrine of Prajāpati: a woman is not entitled to independence."

sanskrit: stry uvāca bādhate maithunaṃ vipra mama bhaktiṃ ca paśya vai adharmaṃ prāpsyase vipra yan māṃ tvaṃ nābhinandasi
english: The woman said: "Desire torments me, O brāhmaṇa; behold too my devotion. You will incur unrighteousness, O brāhmaṇa, in that you will not welcome me."

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca haranti doṣajātāni naraṃ jātaṃ yathecchakam prabhavāmi sadā dhṛtyā bhadre svaṃ śayanaṃ vraja
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: "Faults that are born within carry a man off wherever they will once they arise; but I am ever master of myself through firmness. Go, good lady, to your own couch."

sanskrit: stry uvāca śirasā praṇame vipra prasādaṃ kartum arhasi bhūmau nipatamānāyāḥ śaraṇaṃ bhava me 'nagha
english: The woman said: "With my head I bow, O brāhmaṇa; deign to show me grace. To me who am falling to the ground, be my refuge, O sinless one."

sanskrit: yadi vā doṣajātaṃ tvaṃ paradāreṣu paśyasi ātmānaṃ sparśayāmy adya pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīṣva me dvija
english: "But if you see a fault arising in approaching another man's wife, then this day I make a gift of myself: take my hand, O brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: na doṣo bhavitā caiva satyenaitad bravīmy aham svatantrāṃ māṃ vijānīhi yo 'dharmaḥ so 'stu vai mayi
english: "And no fault shall there be—this I tell you in truth. Know me to be my own mistress; whatever unrighteousness there be, let it rest upon me."

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca svatantrā tvaṃ kathaṃ bhadre brūhi kāraṇam atra vai nāsti loke hi kā cit strī yā vai svātantryam arhati
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: "How are you your own mistress, good lady? Tell me the reason for this. There is no woman in the world who is entitled to independence."

sanskrit: pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane putrāś ca sthavirībhāve na strī svātantryam arhati
english: "In childhood the father protects her, in youth the husband, and in old age the sons; a woman is not entitled to independence."

sanskrit: stry uvāca kaumāraṃ brahmacaryaṃ me kanyaivāsmi na saṃśayaḥ kuru mā vimatiṃ vipra śraddhāṃ vijahi mā mama
english: The woman said: "Mine is the chastity of girlhood; I am yet a maiden, without doubt. Harbor no misgiving, O brāhmaṇa; do not cast away your faith in me."

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca yathā mama tathā tubhyaṃ yathā tava tathā mama jijñāseyam ṛṣes tasya vighnaḥ satyaṃ nu kiṃ bhavet
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: "As it is for me, so it is for you; as it is for you, so for me. Let me probe this: is this hindrance to the seer real, or what?

sanskrit: āścaryaṃ paramaṃ hīdaṃ kiṃ nu śreyo hi me bhavet divyābharaṇavastrā hi kanyeyaṃ mām upasthitā
english: "For this is a thing of the utmost wonder. What course would be best for me? This maiden, decked in celestial ornaments and garments, has come before me."

sanskrit: kiṃ tv asyāḥ paramaṃ rūpaṃ jīrṇam āsīt kathaṃ punaḥ kanyārūpam ihādyaiva kim ihātrottaraṃ bhavet
english: "But how was her surpassing beauty aged before, and how again has she now this very day the form of a maiden? What can be the answer to this?"

sanskrit: yathā paraṃ śaktidhṛter na vyutthāsye kathaṃ cana na rocaye hi vyutthānaṃ dhṛtyaivaṃ sādhayāmy aham
english: "Yet so far as my strength of resolve avails, I shall in no wise swerve; for swerving I deem not good. By steadfastness thus do I prevail."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na bibheti kathaṃ sā strī śāpasya paramadyuteḥ kathaṃ nivṛtto bhagavāṃs tad bhavān prabravītu me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was it that the woman did not fear the curse of one so resplendent? And how did the venerable one desist? Tell me this, I pray.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca aṣṭāvakro 'nvapṛcchat tāṃ rūpaṃ vikuruṣe katham na cānṛtaṃ te vaktavyaṃ brūhi brāhmaṇakāmyayā
english: Bhīṣma said: Aṣṭāvakra questioned her: "How is it that you change your form? You must speak no falsehood; tell me, out of regard for a brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: stry uvāca dyāvāpṛthivīmātraiṣā kāmyā brāhmaṇasattama śṛṇuṣvāvahitaḥ sarvaṃ yad idaṃ satyavikrama
english: The woman said: "This desire of mine is as boundless as heaven and earth, O best of brāhmaṇas. Listen attentively to all of it, O you of truthful valor."

sanskrit: uttarāṃ māṃ diśaṃ viddhi dṛṣṭaṃ strīcāpalaṃ ca te avyutthānena te lokā jitāḥ satyaparākrama
english: "Know me to be the Northern Quarter. The fickleness of women has been shown to you; and by your not swerving, the heavenly worlds have been won by you, O you whose valor is truth."

sanskrit: jijñāseyaṃ prayuktā me sthirīkartuṃ tavānagha sthavirāṇām api strīṇāṃ bādhate maithunajvaraḥ
english: "This testing was set in motion by me to make you steadfast, O sinless one—for even in aged women the fever of desire still torments."

sanskrit: tuṣṭaḥ pitāmahas te 'dya tathā devāḥ savāsavāḥ sa tvaṃ yena ca kāryeṇa saṃprāpto bhagavān iha
english: "The Grandsire is pleased with you this day, and so are the gods together with Vāsava. And as for the purpose for which you, venerable one, have come here—

sanskrit: preṣitas tena vipreṇa kanyāpitrā dvijarṣabha tavopadeśaṃ kartuṃ vai tac ca sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā
english: "sent by that brāhmaṇa, the father of the maiden, O bull among the twice-born, to make the instruction known to you—all of that has been accomplished by me."

sanskrit: kṣemī gamiṣyasi gṛhāñ śramaś ca na bhaviṣyati kanyāṃ prāpsyasi tāṃ vipra putriṇī ca bhaviṣyati
english: "Safe shall you go to your home, and weariness shall not come upon you. You shall win that maiden, O brāhmaṇa, and she shall bear you sons."

sanskrit: kāmyayā pṛṣṭavāṃs tvaṃ māṃ tato vyāhṛtam uttaram anatikramaṇīyaiṣā kṛtsnair lokais tribhiḥ sadā
english: "You questioned me out of desire, and so the answer was uttered—an answer that can never be gainsaid by all the three worlds together."

sanskrit: gacchasva sukṛtaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ vānyac chrotum icchasi yāvad bravīmi viprarṣe aṣṭāvakra yathātatham
english: "Go now, your good work done. Or is there aught else you wish to hear, that I may tell it truly, O seer among brāhmaṇas, Aṣṭāvakra?"

sanskrit: ṛṣiṇā prasāditā cāsmi tava hetor dvijarṣabha tasya saṃmānanārthaṃ me tvayi vākyaṃ prabhāṣitam
english: "I have been entreated by the seer on your behalf, O bull among the twice-born; and to do him honor these words of mine were spoken to you."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasyāḥ sa vipraḥ prāñjaliḥ sthitaḥ anujñātas tayā cāpi svagṛhaṃ punar āvrajat
english: Having heard her words, the brāhmaṇa stood with palms joined; and, taking leave of her, he made his way back to his own home.

sanskrit: gṛham āgamya viśrāntaḥ svajanaṃ pratipūjya ca abhyagacchata taṃ vipraṃ nyāyataḥ kurunandana
english: Having come home and rested, and having honored his kinsfolk, he went duly to that brāhmaṇa, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaś ca tena vipreṇa dṛṣṭaṃ tv etan nidarśanam prāha vipraṃ tadā vipraḥ suprītenāntarātmanā
english: And being questioned by that brāhmaṇa, "Has this token been seen?", the brāhmaṇa then spoke to the brāhmaṇa with a heart well pleased:

sanskrit: bhavatāham anujñātaḥ prasthito gandhamādanam tasya cottarato deśe dṛṣṭaṃ tad daivataṃ mahat
english: "Granted leave by you, I set out for Gandhamādana; and in the region to the north of it I beheld that mighty deity."

sanskrit: tayā cāham anujñāto bhavāṃś cāpi prakīrtitaḥ śrāvitaś cāpi tad vākyaṃ gṛham abhyāgataḥ prabho
english: "And, granted leave by her, with you too made known to her, and having been told her saying, I have come home, my lord."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato vipraḥ pratigṛhṇīṣva me sutām nakṣatratithisaṃyoge pātraṃ hi paramaṃ bhavān
english: Then the brāhmaṇa said to him: "Receive my daughter, when star and lunar day are in conjunction; for you are a most worthy recipient."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca aṣṭāvakras tathety uktvā pratigṛhya ca tāṃ prabho kanyāṃ paramadharmātmā prītimāṃś cābhavat tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: Aṣṭāvakra, saying "So be it," and accepting that maiden, O lord—he of the highest righteousness—was then filled with joy.

sanskrit: kanyāṃ tāṃ pratigṛhyaiva bhāryāṃ paramaśobhanām uvāsa muditas tatra āśrame sve gatajvaraḥ
english: Having received that maiden as his most beautiful wife, he dwelt there gladly in his own hermitage, his fever of doubt now gone.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kim āhur bharataśreṣṭha pātraṃ viprāḥ sanātanam brāhmaṇaṃ liṅginaṃ caiva brāhmaṇaṃ vāpy aliṅginam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whom, O best of the Bhāratas, do the brāhmaṇas declare to be from of old a worthy recipient—the brāhmaṇa who bears the outward marks, or the brāhmaṇa without them?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca svavṛttim abhipannāya liṅgine vetarāya vā deyam āhur mahārāja ubhāv etau tapasvinau
english: Bhīṣma said: To one who keeps to his proper conduct, whether he bears the marks or not, a gift should be given, O great king; for both of these are men of austerity.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śraddhayā parayā pūto yaḥ prayacched dvijātaye havyaṃ kavyaṃ tathā dānaṃ ko doṣaḥ syāt pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a man, purified by the highest faith, presents to a twice-born the offering to the gods, the offering to the ancestors, and gifts, what fault could there be, O Grandsire?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śraddhāpūto naras tāta durdānto 'pi na saṃśayaḥ pūto bhavati sarvatra kiṃ punas tvaṃ mahīpate
english: Bhīṣma said: A man purified by faith, my son, even though he be hard to discipline, becomes pure in every way, without doubt—how much more, then, do you, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca na brāhmaṇaṃ parīkṣeta daiveṣu satataṃ naraḥ kavyapradāne tu budhāḥ parīkṣyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: In rites to the gods a man should never examine the brāhmaṇa; but in the giving of offerings to the ancestors, the wise hold that the brāhmaṇa is to be examined.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na brāhmaṇaḥ sādhayate havyaṃ daivāt prasidhyati devaprasādād ijyante yajamānā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: It is not the brāhmaṇa who brings the offering to fulfillment; it succeeds by the gods' ordinance. By the grace of the gods the sacrificers obtain their fruit, without doubt.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā bharataśreṣṭha satataṃ brahmavādinaḥ mārkaṇḍeyaḥ purā prāha iha lokeṣu buddhimān
english: The brāhmaṇas, O best of the Bhāratas, are ever expounders of the sacred word; thus did the wise Mārkaṇḍeya declare of old here among the worlds.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca apūrvo 'py atha vā vidvān saṃbandhī vātha yo bhavet tapasvī yajñaśīlo vā kathaṃ pātraṃ bhavet tu saḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whether a man be a stranger or a learned one, or a kinsman, or an ascetic, or one given to sacrifice—how is it that such a one becomes a worthy recipient?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kulīnaḥ karmakṛd vaidyas tathā cāpy ānṛśaṃsyavān hrīmān ṛjuḥ satyavādī pātraṃ pūrve ca te trayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Wellborn, performing his rites, learned in the Veda, compassionate, modest, upright, truthful—such a one is a worthy recipient; and the first three among these qualities are foremost.

sanskrit: tatredaṃ śṛṇu me pārtha caturṇāṃ tejasāṃ matam pṛthivyāḥ kāśyapasyāgner mārkaṇḍeyasya caiva hi
english: On this point hear from me, O Pārtha, the judgment of four glorious beings—of the Earth, of Kāśyapa, of Agni, and of Mārkaṇḍeya.

sanskrit: pṛthivy uvāca yathā mahārṇave kṣiptaḥ kṣipraṃ loṣṭo vinaśyati tathā duścaritaṃ sarvaṃ trayy āvṛttyā vinaśyati
english: The Earth said: As a clod of earth cast into the great ocean swiftly dissolves away, so all ill conduct is dissolved away by the recitation of the threefold Veda.

sanskrit: kāśyapa uvāca sarve ca vedāḥ saha ṣaḍbhir aṅgaiḥ; sāṃkhyaṃ purāṇaṃ ca kule ca janma naitāni sarvāṇi gatir bhavanti; śīlavyapetasya narasya rājan
english: Kāśyapa said: All the Vedas together with their six limbs, the Sāṃkhya, the Purāṇa, and birth in a noble line—none of these, all of them together, become a refuge for the man who is bereft of good character, O king.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca adhīyānaḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamāno; yo vidyayā hanti yaśaḥ pareṣām brahman sa tenācarate brahmahatyāṃ; lokās tasya hy antavanto bhavanti
english: Agni said: He who, learned in the texts and accounting himself a sage, destroys the renown of others by his learning—by that, O brāhmaṇa, he commits the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, and his heavenly worlds come to an end.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam nābhijānāmi yady asya satyasyārdham avāpnuyāt
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: A thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were weighed in the balance; and I do not find that the one would attain even to half of that truth.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktvā te jagmur āśu catvāro 'mitatejasaḥ pṛthivī kāśyapo 'gniś ca prakṛṣṭāyuś ca bhārgavaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, those four of boundless splendor swiftly departed—the Earth, Kāśyapa, Agni, and the long-lived scion of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ brāhmaṇā loke vratino bhuñjate haviḥ bhuktaṃ brāhmaṇakāmāya kathaṃ tat sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When brāhmaṇas in the world who keep their vows eat the sacrificial offering, that offering eaten for the sake of a brāhmaṇa—how does it become a meritorious deed?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ādiṣṭino ye rājendra brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ bhuñjate brahmakāmāya vrataluptā bhavanti te
english: Bhīṣma said: Those brāhmaṇas, O king of kings, learned to the end of the Veda, who, being invited, eat for the sake of a brāhmaṇa—they become fallen from their vows.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca anekāntaṃ bahudvāraṃ dharmam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ kiṃ niścitaṃ bhavet tatra tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The wise call dharma many-sided and of many doors. What in it may be held as certain? Tell me that, O Grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ahiṃsā satyam akrodha ānṛśaṃsyaṃ damas tathā ārjavaṃ caiva rājendra niścitaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam
english: Bhīṣma said: Non-injury, truth, freedom from anger, compassion, self-restraint, and uprightness—this, O king of kings, is the certain mark of dharma.

sanskrit: ye tu dharmaṃ praśaṃsantaś caranti pṛthivīm imām anācarantas tad dharmaṃ saṃkare niratāḥ prabho
english: But those who go about this earth praising dharma while not practicing that dharma, devoted to confusion of duties, O lord—

sanskrit: tebhyo ratnaṃ hiraṇyaṃ vā gām aśvān vā dadāti yaḥ daśa varṣāṇi viṣṭhāṃ sa bhuṅkte nirayam āśritaḥ
english: he who gives to them a jewel, or gold, or a cow, or horses—for ten years he feeds upon filth, lodged in hell.

sanskrit: medānāṃ pulkasānāṃ ca tathaivāntāvasāyinām kṛtaṃ karmākṛtaṃ cāpi rāgamohena jalpatām
english: Of the meda outcastes, of the pulkasas, and likewise of those who dwell at the cremation-ground, the rite performed is as good as unperformed, since they babble out of passion and delusion.

sanskrit: vaiśvadevaṃ ca ye mūḍhā viprāya brahmacāriṇe dadatīha na rājendra te lokān bhuñjate 'śubhān
english: And those fools who give the Vaiśvadeva offering to a brāhmaṇa who is a student of the sacred word—nay, O king of kings, they go to enjoy worlds of ill.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ paraṃ brahmacaryasya kiṃ paraṃ dharmalakṣaṇam kiṃ ca śreṣṭhatamaṃ śaucaṃ tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is the highest form of chastity, what the highest mark of dharma, and what the most excellent purity? Tell me that, O Grandsire.
